rule: Two releases may only be compared area by area when the areas are established
to be the same ground. A shared GEOID is not that evidence: identifiers are
reused across vintages even when a boundary moves.
Equivalence can be established in exactly three ways:
1. Same boundary vintage. The areas are identical by construction.
2. Documented provider correspondence: a statement from the data provider
that the areas in the two vintages correspond, recorded below with the
document it rests on.
3. Scoped reviewed evidence: a human examined specific areas and recorded
what they examined, when, and which areas the finding covers.
A computed footprint comparison is NOT one of these ways. It is a measurement.
It can show decisively that two renderings disagree, but two renderings
agreeing within a tolerance does not show that the provider defines them as
the same area, and summary statistics are weaker still: a square and a
diamond of equal area about the same point agree on area and centroid while
describing different ground. Run it to inform a review, not to replace one:
python -m census_explorer.cli geography footprint --a <release> --b <release> --level <level>
With no record below, every cross-vintage comparison is refused. That is the
intended default. Single-period exploration, and comparison between places
within one release, are unaffected.
